lb-msv0.title: Add tested 2048 engine
lb-msv0.description: Goal: Implement the complete 2048 game mechanics as reusable, tested TypeScript logic. Context: SPEC.md and .trapper_keeper/pages/2048-game-overview.md describe the rules. The current app is an Expo TypeScript scaffold with App.tsx as a placeholder. Requirements: Add a small game engine module outside React components, for example under src/game/. Define types for board/cells/directions/game state. Implement new game setup with injectable RNG/spawn choice support, moves in all four directions, merge-once-per-tile behavior, score delta calculation, valid move detection, spawning exactly one tile after valid moves, no spawn after invalid moves, win detection when 2048 is created, and game-over detection when no moves remain. Add a test setup appropriate for the existing Expo/TypeScript project and write focused automated tests for initial setup, left/right/up/down movement, chained merge prevention, invalid moves, score updates, win detection, and game-over detection. Ensure npm test runs the mechanics tests. Acceptance: npm test passes. The engine is exported from a stable module path and is not coupled to React UI. App.tsx may remain a placeholder. Changes are committed and the task is closed. Out of scope: Do not build the visual board, gesture handling, persistence, animations, or full app UI integration.

lb-p961.title: Implement 2048 game mechanics
lb-p961.description: Goal: Add the complete local 2048 gameplay rules core for the My2048 app. Context: SPEC.md defines the game behavior. The Expo scaffold is in place. This feature should establish the tested engine that later UI work can call. Requirements: Keep game logic separate from React components. Represent board state and moves clearly. Support new game creation, four-direction movement, merge-once-per-tile semantics, score deltas, valid/invalid move detection, random tile spawn injection, win detection, and game-over detection. Acceptance: The mechanics are implemented in reusable TypeScript modules with automated tests covering the core rules from SPEC.md. Out of scope: Visual tile UI, gestures, persistence, animations, and React screen integration beyond whatever is needed for exports.

lb-tbxl.title: Add move game-over regression test
lb-tbxl.description: Goal: Add a focused regression test proving move() marks gameOver true when a valid final move plus spawn leaves the board with no legal moves. Context: Review of the merged 2048 engine found no rule bugs, but noted that game-over-after-move behavior is not directly covered. The engine is in src/game/engine.ts and tests are in src/game/engine.test.ts. Requirements: Add the smallest test needed to cover move() recomputing gameOver after a valid move and spawn. Use deterministic chooseSpawn support. Do not change engine behavior unless the test exposes a real bug. Acceptance: npm test passes. The new test would fail if move() did not set state.gameOver after the final valid move. Changes are committed and task is closed. Out of scope: UI integration, broader refactors, spawn API validation, or additional game features.

lb-wdfa.title: Scaffold Expo hello world app
lb-wdfa.description: Goal: Create the initial Expo React Native app scaffold at the repository root and make it boot to a simple My2048 placeholder screen. Context: SPEC.md defines a React Native phone app for 2048. AGENTS.md requires all future mrmouth invocations in this repo to use --codex. The repo is single-purpose, so scaffold at the root rather than under a subdirectory. Requirements: Use Expo with TypeScript if the standard scaffold supports it cleanly. Add the normal Expo project files and package scripts. Make the first screen display a basic My2048/hello-world style placeholder only. Add README.md run instructions for installing dependencies and starting Expo. Keep generated project structure conventional. Acceptance: The repo has a working Expo entry point, package metadata/scripts, and README instructions. Running the documented start command should launch the Expo dev server. The rendered first screen is a simple My2048 placeholder. Changes are committed. Out of scope: Do not implement 2048 game logic, tile UI, persistence, scoring, gestures, or animations.
